data.exact_reserve_text: Net prior year reserves on US casualty business were strengthened during 2023, a common trend seen across the market.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Inwards RITC transferred the 2017-2019 years' liabilities to the syndicate (premium received deemed fair value), increasing gross claims outstanding by the value of the transferred liabilities.

data.standardized_narrative: Gross claims outstanding increased from GBP 55.574m at 1 January 2023 to GBP 111.510m at 31 December 2023 (gross increase of GBP 56.161m). The movement reflects acquisition and recognition of long-duration liabilities (including the prior inwards RITC transfers) and reserve strengthening, notably on US casualty business. The syndicate also implemented an explicit uplift to claims reserves to allow for inflationary pressures.
raw_causal_phrases: Net prior year reserves on US casualty business were strengthened during 2023, a common trend seen across the market.
resulting in an explicit uplift to claims reserves of GBP 2.2m.

On 10th February 2022 and with effect from 1st January 2022, an inwards RITC was completed for Syndicate 2689, for 2017, 2018 & 2019 years of account. A premium of GBP 75,243k ($101,578k) was received. The Syndicate's accounting policy is not to recognise RITC premiums through profit or loss, see the reinsurance to close accounting policy.
data.data_quality_notes: No explicit gross 'prior year only' reserve movement figure was presented. The reported gross 'change in the provision for claims in the year' (GBP 56,161k) has been used as the prior year development (gross) and may include current-year movements and be affected by the 2022 inwards RITC (which materially increased opening/closing balances). A net prior-year strengthening on US casualty is stated but not quantified on a gross basis. Triangle and movement tables in the accounts appear distorted by RITC entries; therefore the prior year movement figure should be treated as indicative.
